crm_notes: Company: Nova Cortech — telematics + edge analytics for fleet management.

AE summary: enterprise procurement - heavy emphasis on deterministic throughput and predictable monthly cost. CFO wants capitalized reserved commitment, infra team insists on clear burst envelope and VPC peering behaviour.
Quote from CTO: 'We need hard guarantees for tokens/sec during peak ingest windows; occasional brief bursts ok but must not cause tail latency spikes.'
Primary workload: live telemetry event enrichment (reranking + small LLM prompts) plus support assistant for field ops.

Desired commercial model: reserved GPU pool (monthly commit) + controlled burst policy with clear overage pricing; prefer a hybrid Dedicated+Private deployment (control plane in Redwood, GPU pool in their VPC).
throughput_requirements: Committed minimum throughput: 120,000–150,000 input tokens/sec aggregated across the Dedicated pool (p99 measurement window, 5m).
Concurrency targets: sustain 64 concurrent real-time sessions with stable latency; soft concurrency cap at 128 for burst events.
Burst policy requested: short bursts up to 2x baseline for 60 seconds, permitted twice per hour; bursts beyond that billed at agreed overage rate.
Latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end token latency <= 350ms for 32-token responses; p99 <= 900ms under committed throughput. SLA to include credits for missed windows.

Reserved GPU planning: initial reservation sized for 8x A100-80GB equivalent; ability to scale to 12 GPUs within 72 hours on contractual addendum. Prefer explicit GPU-to-token-rate mapping in contract.
Fallback & routing: automatic fallback to a quantized v2 model when pool utilization > 95% and burst queue exceeds 60s; fidelity-loss clause to cap acceptable regression.
negotiation_notes: Redwood proposed baseline: 100k tokens/sec committed, 4xA100 equivalent pool; Nova pushing for 120k+ and 8 GPUs — counterrequested price schedule for 8 vs 12 GPUs.
Billing model under discussion: blended fixed monthly commit + per-token overage for bursts. Nova asks for a capped monthly overage and first-30-days free buffer for go-live stabilization.
SLA credits: Nova wants rolling credit calculation per calendar day if p99 > agreed threshold for more than two 5m windows; Redwood proposed monthly credit buckets — mismatch to reconcile.

Ops requirements: detailed runbook for failover (region fallback) and a playbook for controlled degradation (routing to smaller model). Redwood offered automatic routing; Nova requests explicit switchback criteria.
Security/legal: DPA + data residency appendices requested; legal asked for encryption-at-rest mechanics and KMS integration details (Drive doc linked).
